sourceHtml:
If you pay an API bill for an open-weight model, you may wonder whether your own GPU would cost less. GPU rent is charged every hour, busy or idle, while an API charges only for the tokens you use.

A self-hosted LLM costs less only when your traffic keeps the GPU busy enough of the time. At October 8, 2026 prices, a 27B model on one rented RTX 3090 breaks even at about 12% load, while a large mixture-of-experts model on rented H200s never beats the cheapest zero-data-retention (ZDR) API endpoint.

This post works out the break-even with live per-provider prices from our API, then shows how our data controls cover privacy.

TL;DR

  • Break-even load is the GPU’s hourly rent divided by what the same hour of tokens would cost through the API. Below that load, the API is cheaper.

  • DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on four rented H200s never breaks even against the cheapest ZDR endpoint. On two B200s, it needs 76% load at the lowest rent we found.

  • At October 8 prices, Qwen3.8 27B on one RTX 3090 at $0.50 an hour breaks even at 6 to 12% load, but each user gets only about 15 tokens per second.

  • Published self-hosting costs of around a cent per million tokens mostly count cached input tokens, which are nearly free through the API too.

  • Most privacy requirements don’t need self-hosting. provider.zdr limits a request to zero-data-retention endpoints, and our EU and US domains keep requests in-region.

How do you work out whether self-hosting pays off?

Take one hour of a GPU’s time and price it two ways. On one side is the rent. On the other is what the API would charge for the tokens that GPU can serve in an hour, at a speed your users accept.

break-even load = GPU rent per hour / API cost of one fully loaded GPU-hour of tokens

A break-even of 30% means the GPU has to be busy for 30% of the hours you rent it before it costs less than the API. Anything above 100% means the API wins even if the GPU never rests.

Both sides have to be priced on the same token mix, because input, cached input and output tokens have very different API prices. We also left out engineering time and the spare capacity you’d keep for traffic peaks, so every break-even in this post is a lower bound.

What does the API cost for the same open-weight model?

Most open-weight models are served by many providers. Each one runs its own copy of the weights on its own hardware and sets its own price. Our endpoints API (GET /api/v1/models/{author}/{slug}/endpoints) returns every provider’s price and precision for a model, and GET /api/v1/endpoints/zdr lists the endpoints with a ZDR policy. As of October 8, 2026, they returned:

ModelEndpoints (ZDR)Input $/MCached input $/MOutput $/M
qwen/qwen3.8-27b18 (14)0.024 to 0.990.02 to 0.991.49 to 5.25
deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash31 (24)0.016 to 0.450.0007 to 0.200.14 to 1.80

For the same weights, the most expensive provider charges 3.5 times the cheapest for Qwen3.8 27B output, and nearly 13 times for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. A break-even worked out against a single list price can be far off. Providers also serve different precisions, from fp4 to bf16, and our LLM quantization post measures how much that changes the answers.

What we paid for real workloads

Reasoning models spend output tokens thinking before they answer, and agents resend their whole context every turn. So we ran two workloads per model with ZDR enforced and priced each request with GET /api/v1/generation, which reports the tokens and cost the provider actually billed:

WorkloadModelRequestsInput tokens (% cached)Output tokens (% reasoning)CostPer 1M output tokens
Chat over a 5k-token documentDeepSeek V4.1 Flash1053,330 (68%)12,476 (97%)$0.0110$0.88
8-turn agent, 60k-token contextDeepSeek V4.1 Flash8504,747 (75%)28,509 (83%)$0.0243$0.85
Chat over a 5k-token documentQwen3.8 27B1072,329 (56%)25,084 (97%)$0.0694$2.77
7-turn agent, 85k-token contextQwen3.8 27B7595,223 (100%)81,870 (99%)$0.1900$2.32

The last column divides the full cost, input included, by the output tokens. Almost every output token was reasoning, and a self-hosted copy of the model would spend the same GPU time producing them. Qwen3.8 27B also hit our 16,000-token cap while still thinking on 3 of its 7 agent turns. Every API run for this post cost $0.49 in total.

What does a self-hosted LLM cost to run?

We didn’t rent these GPUs ourselves. The self-hosted side uses published benchmarks and rental prices, so treat each row as an assumption:

SetupThroughput per GPUSourceRent per GPU-hour
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, 4x H200, vLLM fp4, 32 concurrent sessions35,084 input + 231 output tok/s, 95% of input cached, 71 tok/s per userInferenceX agentic traces, 2026-09-21$2.90 (InferenceX retail tier), $4.59 (RunPod)
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, 2x B200, vLLM fp4, 32 concurrent sessions117,225 input + 683 output tok/s, 96% cached, 232 tok/s per userInferenceX, 2026-10-03$3.70 (InferenceX retail), $6.79 (RunPod), $6.89 (Lambda)
Qwen3.8 27B, 1x RTX 3090, vLLM W4A16, 64 concurrent942 output tok/s at 128 tokens in / 512 out, about 15 tok/s per userHyperQwen benchmarks$0.50 (RunPod), or about $0.05 in power for a card you own (250 W at the EIA July 2026 US residential rate)

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash has 552B backbone parameters, so it needs a multi-GPU node. Qwen3.8 27B is a dense model that fits on one 24 GB card at 4 bits.

Throughput is per GPU, the way InferenceX reports it, so every cost in this post is per GPU-hour. Per-user speed counts only the time a response is being generated, and these agentic sessions spend much of their time on prefill, so it doesn’t multiply out to the total. The 3090 figure comes from HyperQwen’s heavily patched vLLM build, so treat it as a best case.

We used its end-to-end figure, which includes prefill, rather than its 1,035 tok/s decode-only headline. HyperQwen benchmarked 128-token prompts, and our chat prompts are much longer, so for our chat mix we estimated 565 output tokens per second from its measured prefill and decode rates.

When does self-hosting pay off?

For each setup, we took the hour of tokens the benchmark measured, split it into uncached input, cached input and output, and priced that mix at every ZDR endpoint for the model, then divided the rent by the result. API prices are from October 8, 2026:

SetupRent per GPU-hourAPI cost of the same hour, cheapest ZDR / median ZDRBreak-even load vs cheapest ZDRBreak-even load vs median ZDR
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, 4x H200$2.90$1.70 / $3.54never82%
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, 4x H200$4.59$1.70 / $3.54nevernever
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, 2x B200$3.70$4.87 / $9.9576%37%
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, 2x B200$6.79$4.87 / $9.95never68%
Qwen3.8 27B, 1x RTX 3090, short prompts$0.50$5.89 / $8.358%6%
Qwen3.8 27B, 1x RTX 3090, our chat mix (estimated)$0.50$4.33 / $6.1412%8%
Qwen3.8 27B, own RTX 3090, power only$0.05$5.89 / $8.351%1%

“Never” means the rent is higher than the API cost even at 100% load. Prices move quickly. On October 19, a new ZDR endpoint for Qwen3.8 27B charged $0.50 per million output tokens, which moves the short-prompt break-even to about 29%.

Start from the load you actually have. Traffic that only arrives during working hours, 40 of the week’s 168 hours, keeps a GPU busy at most 24% of the time. At October 8 prices, that rules out every DeepSeek row and leaves the 3090. Against the October 19 endpoint, the 3090 would need about 29%, so check current prices before you buy. A batch pipeline running around the clock can reach 70%, which brings both B200 rows into range against the median ZDR price, but neither against the cheapest.

In monthly terms, the rented 3090 costs $365 and pays for itself after about 170 million output tokens of our chat mix. The two-B200 node costs $5,402 a month at retail rent and has to serve 2.7 billion output tokens before it beats the cheapest ZDR endpoint.

The small model comes out ahead because its API prices are high compared with the hardware it needs. Providers charge $1.49 to $5.25 per million output tokens for Qwen3.8 27B, and a $0.50-an-hour card produces about 3.4 million of them an hour. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is the opposite case. Twenty-four ZDR endpoints compete for its traffic, and the cheapest charges $0.18 per million output tokens.

The 3090’s low cost comes with a speed trade-off. It reaches that throughput by serving 64 requests at once, at about 15 tokens per second each. That’s slow for a chat interface, and slower still for a reasoning model that writes thousands of hidden tokens before its answer. Across the 18 API endpoints for Qwen3.8 27B, the median ran at 45 tokens per second in the 30 minutes before our pull, and the fastest at 474.

Why do published self-hosting costs look so low?

If you’ve seen self-hosting quoted at around a cent per million tokens, the token mix is usually the reason. InferenceX puts DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on H200 at $0.012 per million tokens at hyperscaler pricing. That figure is per million total tokens, and in its agentic workload, 99% of tokens are input, 95% of them served from the prefix cache. Through the API, cached input for that model costs $0.0007 to $0.20 per million, so those tokens are cheap either way.

Priced per output token, the same H200 at the $2.90 retail rent costs $3.49 per million before any input is counted. The cheapest ZDR endpoint charges $0.18.

Do you need to self-host for privacy?

Privacy is the other common reason to self-host, and you can get most of it through the API. Setting provider.zdr on a request limits it to endpoints whose providers don’t store your prompts or completions. If your ZDR setting also allows Safety Retention endpoints, those may keep prompts and responses to detect abuse, so choose ZDR only when you need no retention at all. Providers with implicit caching may also hold derived KV-cache data for a short time, as our implicit caching explainer describes. You can also enforce ZDR account-wide, per model group, or in a guardrail that covers specific API keys. On the Business and Enterprise plans, requests sent to eu.openrouter.ai or us.openrouter.ai run only on endpoints in that region, and they fail rather than leave it.

This script tries both, including two requests we expected to fail:

"""The privacy paths: ZDR per request, a ZDR conflict, and EU in-region routing."""
import os

import requests

KEY = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['OPENROUTER_API_KEY']}"}
MSG = [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with the word ok."}]

def ask(base, model, provider=None):
    body = {"model": model, "messages": MSG, "max_tokens": 400, "provider": provider or {}}
    r = requests.post(f"{base}/api/v1/chat/completions", json=body, headers=KEY, timeout=120)
    data = r.json()
    if r.status_code == 200:
        return f"{r.status_code} served by {data['provider']}"
    return f"{r.status_code} {data['error']['message']}"

GLOBAL, EU = "https://openrouter.ai", "https://eu.openrouter.ai"

print("1. ZDR on, any provider:     ", ask(GLOBAL, "deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash", {"zdr": True}))
print("2. ZDR on, only DeepSeek API:", ask(GLOBAL, "deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash", {"zdr": True, "only": ["deepseek"]}))
print("3. EU domain, DeepSeek:      ", ask(EU, "deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash"))
print("4. EU domain, GLM 5.3 + ZDR: ", ask(EU, "z-ai/glm-5.3", {"zdr": True}))

eu_models = requests.get(f"{GLOBAL}/api/v1/models", params={"region": "eu"}, timeout=60).json()["data"]
print(f"5. models eligible for EU in-region routing: {len(eu_models)}")

Output recorded October 8, 2026:

1. ZDR on, any provider:      200 served by Decart
2. ZDR on, only DeepSeek API: 404 No endpoints found matching your data policy (Zero data retention). Configure: https://openrouter.ai/settings/privacy
3. EU domain, DeepSeek:       404 No endpoints found supporting your data region.
4. EU domain, GLM 5.3 + ZDR:  200 served by Inceptron
5. models eligible for EU in-region routing: 72

Both filters run before we pick a provider, so they shrink the list of candidate endpoints instead of rerouting after the fact. With zdr on, DeepSeek’s own API drops out because it retains data. Pinning the request to that provider with only leaves no endpoint at all, which returns the first 404. The EU domain keeps only endpoints we’ve onboarded in Europe. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash had none, so the third request failed instead of quietly going to the US. To use EU routing, pick a model with EU endpoints from GET /api/v1/models?region=eu, which listed 72 models, including GLM 5.3.

ZDR has one limit. Your prompts are still processed on a provider’s GPU, so it doesn’t give you control of the hardware. If your policy requires the model to run on a deployment you control, Private Endpoints (Enterprise plan) add your own dedicated or fine-tuned deployment to a catalog model’s provider list. It must be hosted with a provider we support for BYOK, your team calls it with the same slug, and public endpoints stay available as fallbacks if you list them. If data must never leave hardware you operate, self-host and size the hardware from the break-even table above. Our ZDR explainer and data residency guide compare the options in more detail.

Can you self-host and use the API together?

Yes, and for most teams the break-even table points to this setup. A GPU only pays off at high load, so size your own for the steady base of your traffic, where it stays busy, and send the peaks to the API, where you pay only for what you use.

This works because vLLM and SGLang expose the same OpenAI-compatible chat API we do. A client moves between them by changing the base URL, key and model name. Fall back to the API on a connection error, or on the 429 or 503 your server returns when its queue is full. Set provider.zdr on the API side so overflow traffic keeps zero data retention. If your policy requires prompts to stay on hardware you control, don’t overflow to the API.

Two things can go wrong with this setup. If your local copy runs at a different precision from the API endpoint, the same prompt can get different answers, so pin the API side to a matching quantization with provider routing. And a conversation that switches backends partway through loses its prompt cache, so keep each conversation on one side once it starts.

Frequently asked questions

Is self-hosting an LLM worth it?

For cost alone, only if you can keep the GPU busy. In our numbers, Qwen3.8 27B on a rented RTX 3090 breaks even at 6 to 12% load. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on rented data-center GPUs needs 37% load or more, and against the cheapest zero data retention endpoint it often never breaks even. Privacy and control can justify self-hosting at any load.

Which LLM is best for self-hosting?

Models that fit on one GPU are the best fit, because they avoid multi-GPU servers and their API prices leave the most room to save. Qwen3.8 27B, for example, runs on one 24 GB card at 4 bits. Our rankings and the open-weight vs closed-weight comparison show which models developers use most.

What is the cheapest self-hosted LLM option?

A GPU you already own. An RTX 3090 limited to 250 W costs about $0.05 an hour in electricity at the July 2026 US residential average, so it beats the cheapest zero data retention endpoint for Qwen3.8 27B once it’s busy about 1% of the time. The trade-offs are slower responses for each user and your own time spent on maintenance.

Can I host my own model and still use it through OpenRouter?

Yes, on the Enterprise plan. Private Endpoints route a catalog model’s slug to your own dedicated or fine-tuned deployment, hosted with a provider we support for BYOK. Only the users and organizations you approve can see or call it.

Next steps

  • Zero Data Retention: enforce ZDR per request, per model group, in a guardrail or account-wide.

  • In-Region Routing: send requests through the EU and US domains, and enforce a region with a guardrail.

  • The model pages for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and Qwen3.8 27B list current per-provider prices and throughput.

translation.html:
如果你正在为开放权重模型支付 API 账单，可能会想，用自己的 GPU 会不会更便宜。GPU 租金按小时收取，无论忙闲，而 API 只对你使用的 token 收费。

只有当你的流量能让 GPU 在足够多的时间里保持忙碌时，自托管 LLM 才更便宜。按 2026 年 10 月 8 日的价格，在一张租用的 RTX 3090 上运行 27B 模型，约在 12% 的负载率下达到盈亏平衡；而在租用的 H200 上运行大型混合专家模型，成本始终无法低于最便宜的零数据保留（ZDR）API 端点。

本文使用我们 API 提供的各供应商实时价格计算盈亏平衡点，然后介绍我们的数据控制措施如何满足隐私需求。

要点速览

  • 盈亏平衡负载率等于 GPU 每小时租金除以通过 API 处理同一小时 token 所需的费用。低于这一负载率时，API 更便宜。

  • 在四张租用的 H200 上运行 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash，相对于最便宜的 ZDR 端点，始终无法达到盈亏平衡。在两张 B200 上运行时，按我们找到的最低租金计算，需要达到 76% 的负载率。

  • 按 10 月 8 日的价格，在一张每小时租金为 0.50 美元的 RTX 3090 上运行 Qwen3.8 27B，在 6% 至 12% 的负载率下达到盈亏平衡，但每位用户只能获得约每秒 15 个 token 的速度。

  • 公开资料中每百万 token 约一美分的自托管成本，大多计算的是缓存输入 token，而通过 API 处理这些 token 也几乎免费。

  • 大多数隐私要求并不需要通过自托管来满足。provider.zdr 将请求限制在零数据保留端点，我们的欧盟和美国域名则确保请求留在相应区域内。

如何计算自托管是否划算？

取 GPU 一小时的处理量，用两种方式计价。一边是租金，另一边是在用户可接受的速度下，GPU 一小时能够处理的 token 通过 API 处理所需的费用。

break-even load = GPU rent per hour / API cost of one fully loaded GPU-hour of tokens

盈亏平衡负载率为 30%，意味着 GPU 至少要在租用时间的 30% 里保持忙碌，成本才会低于 API。超过 100% 则意味着，即使 GPU 一刻不停，API 也更便宜。

两边必须按相同的 token 构成计价，因为输入、缓存输入和输出 token 的 API 价格差别很大。我们也没有计入工程时间，以及为流量高峰预留的容量，因此本文中的每个盈亏平衡点都是下限。

通过 API 使用同一个开放权重模型需要多少钱？

大多数开放权重模型都有多家供应商提供服务。每家供应商都在自己的硬件上运行一份模型权重，并自行定价。我们的端点 API（GET /api/v1/models/{author}/{slug}/endpoints）返回某个模型各家供应商的价格和精度，GET /api/v1/endpoints/zdr 则列出采用 ZDR 政策的端点。截至 2026 年 10 月 8 日，它们返回的数据如下：

模型端点数（ZDR）输入价格（美元/百万 token）缓存输入价格（美元/百万 token）输出价格（美元/百万 token）
qwen/qwen3.8-27b18 (14)0.024 至 0.990.02 至 0.991.49 至 5.25
deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash31 (24)0.016 至 0.450.0007 至 0.200.14 至 1.80

对于相同的权重，Qwen3.8 27B 输出 token 最贵供应商的收费是最便宜供应商的 3.5 倍，DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 则接近 13 倍。只按某一个标价计算盈亏平衡点，结果可能偏差很大。供应商提供的精度也各不相同，从 fp4 到 bf16 都有，我们的 LLM 量化文章测量了这会让回答发生多大变化。

真实工作负载的实际费用

推理模型会在回答前消耗输出 token 进行思考，智能体则会在每一轮重新发送完整上下文。因此，我们为每个模型运行了两种工作负载，强制启用 ZDR，并使用 GET /api/v1/generation 为每个请求计价，该接口会报告供应商实际计费的 token 数和费用：

工作负载模型请求数输入 token 数（缓存占比）输出 token 数（推理占比）费用每 100 万输出 token 的费用
围绕一份 5,000 token 的文档聊天DeepSeek V4.1 Flash1053,330 (68%)12,476 (97%)$0.0110$0.88
8 轮智能体任务，60,000 token 上下文DeepSeek V4.1 Flash8504,747 (75%)28,509 (83%)$0.0243$0.85
围绕一份 5,000 token 的文档聊天Qwen3.8 27B1072,329 (56%)25,084 (97%)$0.0694$2.77
7 轮智能体任务，85,000 token 上下文Qwen3.8 27B7595,223 (100%)81,870 (99%)$0.1900$2.32

最后一列用包含输入费用在内的总费用除以输出 token 数。几乎所有输出 token 都用于推理，自托管的同一模型也会花费相同的 GPU 时间来生成它们。Qwen3.8 27B 在 7 轮智能体任务中，有 3 轮在仍然思考时就触及了我们设置的 16,000 token 上限。本文所有 API 运行的费用合计为 0.49 美元。

运行自托管 LLM 需要多少钱？

我们没有亲自租用这些 GPU。自托管部分采用公开的基准测试和租赁价格，因此请将每一行都视为一组假设：

配置每张 GPU 的吞吐量来源每 GPU 小时租金
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash，4 张 H200，vLLM fp4，32 个并发会话每秒 35,084 个输入 token + 231 个输出 token，95% 的输入已缓存，每位用户每秒 71 个 tokenInferenceX 智能体运行轨迹，2026-09-212.90 美元（InferenceX 零售档），4.59 美元（RunPod）
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash，2 张 B200，vLLM fp4，32 个并发会话每秒 117,225 个输入 token + 683 个输出 token，96% 已缓存，每位用户每秒 232 个 tokenInferenceX，2026-10-033.70 美元（InferenceX 零售），6.79 美元（RunPod），6.89 美元（Lambda）
Qwen3.8 27B，1 张 RTX 3090，vLLM W4A16，64 路并发输入 128 个 token、输出 512 个 token 时，每秒输出 942 个 token，每位用户约每秒 15 个 tokenHyperQwen 基准测试0.50 美元（RunPod）；如果显卡为自有，电费约为 0.05 美元（功耗 250 W，按 EIA 公布的 2026 年 7 月美国居民电价计算）

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 有 552B 个主干参数，因此需要多 GPU 节点。Qwen3.8 27B 是稠密模型，采用 4 位量化时可放入一张 24 GB 显卡。

吞吐量按每张 GPU 计算，与 InferenceX 的报告方式一致，因此本文所有成本都以每 GPU 小时为单位。每位用户的速度只计算生成响应的时间，而这些智能体会话的大量时间用于预填充，因此将每位用户的速度相乘并不能得到总吞吐量。3090 的数据来自 HyperQwen 大幅修改过的 vLLM 版本，因此应将其视为最佳情况。

我们采用了其包含预填充的端到端数据，而非其重点宣传的仅解码阶段每秒 1,035 个 token。HyperQwen 的基准测试使用 128 token 的提示词，而我们的聊天提示词长得多，因此针对我们的聊天 token 构成，我们根据它实测的预填充和解码速率，估算出每秒输出 565 个 token。

自托管何时划算？

对于每种配置，我们取基准测试测得的一小时 token 处理量，将其拆分为未缓存输入、缓存输入和输出，再按该模型每个 ZDR 端点的价格为这一构成计价，最后用租金除以所得费用。API 价格取自 2026 年 10 月 8 日：

“无法达到”意味着，即使负载率为 100%，租金仍高于 API 费用。价格变化很快。10 月 19 日，Qwen3.8 27B 新增的一个 ZDR 端点将每百万输出 token 的价格定为 0.50 美元，这使短提示词场景的盈亏平衡负载率升至约 29%。

先看你实际拥有的负载。若流量只在工作时间到来，即一周 168 小时中的 40 小时，GPU 最多只能在 24% 的时间里保持忙碌。按 10 月 8 日的价格，这排除了所有 DeepSeek 配置，只剩下 3090。若与 10 月 19 日的端点相比，3090 需要约 29% 的负载率，因此购买前应查看当前价格。全天候运行的批处理流水线可以达到 70% 的负载率，这让两种 B200 配置相对于 ZDR 价格中位数都能达到盈亏平衡，但相对于最便宜的 ZDR 端点则都不行。

按月计算，租用 3090 的费用为 365 美元，处理约 1.7 亿个符合我们聊天 token 构成的输出 token 后即可达到盈亏平衡。双 B200 节点按零售租金计算每月费用为 5,402 美元，必须处理 27 亿个输出 token，成本才会低于最便宜的 ZDR 端点。

小模型胜出，是因为其 API 价格相对于所需硬件较高。供应商对 Qwen3.8 27B 每百万输出 token 收费 1.49 至 5.25 美元，而一张每小时租金 0.50 美元的显卡每小时能生成约 340 万个输出 token。DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 则相反。24 个 ZDR 端点争夺其流量，其中最便宜的每百万输出 token 收费 0.18 美元。

3090 的低成本伴随着速度上的取舍。它通过同时处理 64 个请求达到这一吞吐量，每个请求约每秒 15 个 token。这对聊天界面来说偏慢；对于需要在给出答案前生成数千个隐藏 token 的推理模型，就更慢了。在 Qwen3.8 27B 的 18 个 API 端点中，我们拉取数据前 30 分钟内的速度中位数为每秒 45 个 token，最快的为每秒 474 个 token。

为什么公开的自托管成本看起来这么低？

如果你见过每百万 token 约一美分的自托管报价，原因通常在于 token 构成。InferenceX 按超大规模云服务商定价计算，在 H200 上运行 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 的成本为每百万 token 0.012 美元。这一数字按总 token 数计算，而在它的智能体工作负载中，99% 的 token 是输入，其中 95% 由前缀缓存提供。通过 API 处理该模型的缓存输入，每百万 token 的费用为 0.0007 至 0.20 美元，因此无论采用哪种方式，这些 token 都很便宜。

若按输出 token 计价，同样的 H200 按 2.90 美元零售租金计算，在尚未计入任何输入的情况下，每百万输出 token 的成本就达到 3.49 美元。最便宜的 ZDR 端点收费为 0.18 美元。

为了隐私，你需要自托管吗？

隐私是自托管的另一个常见原因，而通过 API 也能满足大部分隐私需求。在请求中设置 provider.zdr，会将请求限制到供应商不存储你的提示词或补全内容的端点。如果你的 ZDR 设置也允许 Safety Retention 端点，这些端点可能会保留提示词和响应以检测滥用，因此在需要完全不保留数据时，应选择仅限 ZDR。采用隐式缓存的供应商也可能短暂保留衍生的 KV 缓存数据，具体见我们的隐式缓存说明。你也可以强制启用 ZDR，范围可以是整个账户、每个模型组，或覆盖特定 API 密钥的护栏。在 Business 和 Enterprise 套餐中，发送到 eu.openrouter.ai 或 us.openrouter.ai 的请求只会在相应区域内的端点上运行；如果无法满足，就会失败，而不会离开该区域。

这个脚本会尝试这两种控制措施，其中包括两个我们预期会失败的请求：

"""The privacy paths: ZDR per request, a ZDR conflict, and EU in-region routing."""
import os

import requests

KEY = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['OPENROUTER_API_KEY']}"}
MSG = [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with the word ok."}]

def ask(base, model, provider=None):
    body = {"model": model, "messages": MSG, "max_tokens": 400, "provider": provider or {}}
    r = requests.post(f"{base}/api/v1/chat/completions", json=body, headers=KEY, timeout=120)
    data = r.json()
    if r.status_code == 200:
        return f"{r.status_code} served by {data['provider']}"
    return f"{r.status_code} {data['error']['message']}"

GLOBAL, EU = "https://openrouter.ai", "https://eu.openrouter.ai"

print("1. ZDR on, any provider:     ", ask(GLOBAL, "deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash", {"zdr": True}))
print("2. ZDR on, only DeepSeek API:", ask(GLOBAL, "deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash", {"zdr": True, "only": ["deepseek"]}))
print("3. EU domain, DeepSeek:      ", ask(EU, "deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash"))
print("4. EU domain, GLM 5.3 + ZDR: ", ask(EU, "z-ai/glm-5.3", {"zdr": True}))

eu_models = requests.get(f"{GLOBAL}/api/v1/models", params={"region": "eu"}, timeout=60).json()["data"]
print(f"5. models eligible for EU in-region routing: {len(eu_models)}")

输出记录于 2026 年 10 月 8 日：

1. ZDR on, any provider:      200 served by Decart
2. ZDR on, only DeepSeek API: 404 No endpoints found matching your data policy (Zero data retention). Configure: https://openrouter.ai/settings/privacy
3. EU domain, DeepSeek:       404 No endpoints found supporting your data region.
4. EU domain, GLM 5.3 + ZDR:  200 served by Inceptron
5. models eligible for EU in-region routing: 72

两种筛选都在我们选择供应商之前执行，因此它们会缩小候选端点列表，而不是事后重新路由。启用 zdr 后，DeepSeek 自有 API 会因保留数据而被排除。使用 only 将请求限定到该供应商后，就没有任何可用端点，因此返回第一个 404。欧盟域名只保留我们已在欧洲接入的端点。DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 没有这样的端点，因此第三个请求失败了，而没有悄悄转到美国。要使用欧盟路由，请从 GET /api/v1/models?region=eu 中选择具有欧盟端点的模型，该接口当时列出了 72 个模型，包括 GLM 5.3。

ZDR 有一个局限。你的提示词仍会在供应商的 GPU 上处理，因此它并不能让你掌控硬件。如果你的政策要求模型在由你控制的部署上运行，Private Endpoints（Enterprise 套餐）可以将你自己的专用部署或微调部署加入模型目录中某个模型的供应商列表。该部署必须托管在我们支持 BYOK 的供应商处，你的团队使用相同的 slug 调用它；如果你列出了公共端点，它们仍可作为回退选项。如果数据绝不能离开你运营的硬件，就采用自托管，并根据上面的盈亏平衡表确定硬件规模。我们的 ZDR 说明和数据驻留指南更详细地比较了这些选项。

可以同时使用自托管和 API 吗？

可以，而且对于大多数团队，盈亏平衡表指向的正是这种方案。GPU 只有在高负载下才划算，因此应根据稳定的基础流量配置自有硬件，让它保持忙碌，再将高峰流量发送到 API，按实际用量付费。

这种方式可行，是因为 vLLM 和 SGLang 与我们一样，都提供兼容 OpenAI 的聊天 API。客户端只需更改基础 URL、密钥和模型名称，就能在它们之间切换。在发生连接错误，或服务器因队列已满而返回 429 或 503 时，回退到 API。在 API 端设置 provider.zdr，让溢出流量仍保持零数据保留。如果你的政策要求提示词必须留在你控制的硬件上，就不要将溢出流量发送到 API。

这种方案可能遇到两个问题。如果本地副本与 API 端点采用的精度不同，同一个提示词可能得到不同答案，因此应通过供应商路由将 API 端固定为匹配的量化方式。另外，对话中途切换后端会丢失其提示词缓存，因此每段对话开始后都应保持在同一端。

常见问题

自托管 LLM 值得吗？

单从成本考虑，只有在能让 GPU 保持忙碌时才值得。根据我们的数据，在租用的 RTX 3090 上运行 Qwen3.8 27B，在 6% 至 12% 的负载率下达到盈亏平衡。在租用的数据中心 GPU 上运行 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash，需要 37% 或更高的负载率；与最便宜的零数据保留端点相比，往往始终无法达到盈亏平衡。隐私和控制权可以成为在任何负载率下采用自托管的理由。

哪种 LLM 最适合自托管？

能放进单张 GPU 的模型最合适，因为它们无需多 GPU 服务器，而且其 API 价格留下了最大的节省空间。例如，Qwen3.8 27B 采用 4 位量化时，可在一张 24 GB 显卡上运行。我们的排行榜和开放权重与封闭权重对比展示了开发者最常使用哪些模型。

最便宜的自托管 LLM 方案是什么？

使用你已经拥有的 GPU。按 2026 年 7 月美国居民平均电价计算，将 RTX 3090 的功耗限制在 250 W 时，每小时电费约为 0.05 美元，因此只要它在约 1% 的时间里保持忙碌，运行 Qwen3.8 27B 的成本就低于最便宜的零数据保留端点。代价是每位用户的响应速度较慢，以及你需要投入自己的时间维护。

我可以托管自己的模型，同时仍通过 OpenRouter 使用它吗？

可以，Enterprise 套餐支持。Private Endpoints 将模型目录中某个模型的 slug 路由到你自己的专用部署或微调部署，该部署需托管在我们支持 BYOK 的供应商处。只有你批准的用户和组织才能看到或调用它。
